pages.text: The $(item)Filament Winder$() turns raw materials into Filament Units. Put a $(l)material$() in the input slot and an empty (or partial) $(item)Filament Spool$() in the spool slot; the winder consumes the material and winds its FU onto the spool.$(br2)One universal winder handles $(l)every tier$(): the spool's tier, not the winder, decides what it accepts.
The Filament Winder: string, sticks, and a smooth-stone base. Craftable from Tier 1.

pages.title: What It Accepts
pages.text: The winder enforces the $(l)exact-tier$() rule: a material only winds into a spool of its own tier. If you load a mismatched spool, the GUI shows $(l)"Requires Tier X Spool"$().$(br2)Items with no FU value (un-priced blocks in strict mode) show $(l)"Can't be converted"$() and are left untouched. Bamboo is $(l)recyclable$() now, but trivially-farmable outputs like bones are $(l)held back$() from winding so they can't be laundered into filament (they still print).$(br2)With $(l)Mystical Agradditions$() installed, the $(item)Nether Star$() and $(item)Dragon Egg$() join that list, because that mod adds crops for both and their payouts assume you can't farm them. Only winding changes: the star still crafts, builds beacons and prints. $(l)Insanium$() can be neither wound nor printed. $(l)Without$() that mod, both trophies wind exactly as before.

pages.title: Filament Converter
pages.text: The $(item)Filament Converter$() automates winding: set a filter by right-clicking it with an item, and it pulls that item one at a time from an $(l)adjacent input inventory$() - a chest, a pipe, a hopper, an AE2 $(l)ME Interface$() - converts it, and tops up spools docked on adjacent machines.$(br2)It only converts when a docked spool can take the whole yield, so filament is never stranded, and it honours the winder blacklist.
